public_rationale: There is no deadline. Reporting shows efforts to control token use, but it does not establish the comparative claim that this revenue disappears first. Microsoft's stated focus on impact also cautions against equating spending discipline with revenue disappearance. No decisive event meets the early-resolution rule by October 28, 2026.
limitations: Policy announcements do not measure realized revenue.
The comparison group is an evaluator interpretation.
The claim supplies no accounting basis for a monetary comparison.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: TokenMaxxing spending is exactly the kind of revenue that disappears first.

statement.excerpt: Furthermore, TokenMaxxing is exactly the kind of revenue that disappears first.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is a forecast about the durability of spending driven by maximizing token consumption: customers will withdraw it ahead of other discretionary purchases when reducing costs.
The adjacent cost-cutting discussion supplies the testing circumstance. The sentence does not give a deadline or identify a particular future budget event as an explicit antecedent.
I use comparable discretionary software and AI purchases as a practical comparison group. Zitron does not specify that group.
Removing a leaderboard, limiting usage or switching suppliers does not by itself establish that the associated revenue disappeared first.
criteria.support_condition: Dated records across relevant customers show that spending attributable to tokenmaxxing was withdrawn ahead of comparable discretionary purchases during completed cost-cutting rounds, with corresponding loss of supplier receipts.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show tokenmaxxing spending persisting while other discretionary purchases are withdrawn first, sufficiently broadly to contradict the claimed tendency.
